clinician.trajectory_summary: A 26-year-old male presented with three months of constitutional symptoms including productive cough, fever, night sweats, myalgias, anorexia, and weight loss. Physical examination was unremarkable with no palpable lymphadenopathy. A chest CT scan revealed a large (9 × 10 × 14 cm) necrotic cavitary lesion in the right upper lobe with mediastinal adenopathy. Infectious causes, including fungal, bacterial, and mycobacterial infections, were ruled out by various tests. A CT-guided core needle biopsy of the lesion, performed under strict airborne precautions, confirmed classic Hodgkin lymphoma, mixed cellularity type, with typical Reed–Sternberg cells and positive immunohistochemical staining for CD15, CD30, and PAX-5. Subsequent imaging showed progression of the pulmonary lesions but no intra-abdominal involvement. The patient initiated combined chemotherapy and immunotherapy (doxorubicin, dacarbazine, nivolumab, and brentuximab vedotin), and an interim PET scan showed a favorable response with decreased disease burden.
